questions.question: A campaign has the highest predicted conversion value, but its consent signal cannot be verified before the auction deadline. What should the serving system do?
options: Serve the campaign because the model score is high.
Use the campaign only for users with a high historical click-through rate.
Remove the campaign from this auction and continue with candidates whose required constraints are verified.
Wait indefinitely for the consent service so the model can preserve accuracy.
questions.explanation: Consent is a hard eligibility constraint. A bounded auction can continue with other eligible candidates, but it cannot infer permission from a prediction score or a timeout.

questions.question: At 250,000 peak auctions per second, what online feature-and-rich-scoring load remains when 92% of auctions use a valid precomputed feature path?
options: 2,000 auctions per second
20,000 auctions per second
92,000 auctions per second
230,000 auctions per second
questions.explanation: Eight percent of 250,000 is 20,000. Capacity planning must also consider lower cache coverage, where more work moves to the online path.

questions.question: Which data design most directly prevents feature leakage in an ad-conversion model?
options: Use the latest profile and conversion state for every historical impression.
Include every future conversion so rare outcomes are easier to learn.
Build each training row from an event-time feature snapshot and a label cutoff after the decision time.
Remove impression position so the model only sees clicks.
questions.explanation: Point-in-time snapshots ensure the training example contains only information that could have existed when the ad decision was made.

questions.question: Why should budget reservation happen after final eligibility and before returning the auction winner?
options: It makes the ranking model train faster.
It prevents a campaign from being returned after its remaining budget is concurrently exhausted.
It allows the response to omit a trace ID.
It guarantees the winning price is the highest submitted bid.
questions.explanation: A documented, atomic reservation closes the race between scoring and spend. If it cannot complete, that candidate must be removed before a winner is returned.

questions.question: The personalized feature service is unavailable, but consent, frequency-cap, and budget authorities remain healthy. Which degraded mode is defensible?
options: Serve a contextual ranker using the same hard eligibility gates and log the fallback.
Bypass frequency caps because personalization is already unavailable.
Reuse expired features regardless of consent state.
Retry the feature service until the exchange deadline has elapsed.
questions.explanation: Personalization may degrade to an approved contextual model. The fallback must remain observable and preserve hard constraints rather than trading them for availability.

questions.question: Which release condition best protects against a model that raises aggregate revenue while harming a meaningful audience slice?
options: Promote once overall click-through rate rises for one hour.
Use only advertiser-reported attributed conversions as the decision metric.
Require holdout-based value evidence plus latency, privacy, and slice-level fairness gates with rollback on regression.
Remove the affected slice from evaluation because it lowers the average.
questions.explanation: Aggregate uplift is insufficient. A production release needs counterfactual evidence and explicit operational, privacy, and slice-level stop conditions.
